Now, $$G^{''}$$ is continuous everywhere, and $$G^{''}(t) = 0$$ , when $$t = \frac{15}{2}$$ , giving $$t = \frac{15}{2}$$ as the only candidate for an inflection point of $$G$$ . problem.paragraph: Effect of Advertising on Bank Deposits The following graphs were used by the CEO of the Madison Savings Bank to illustrate what effect a projected promotional campaign would have on its deposits over the next year. The functions $$D_{1}$$ and $$D_{2}$$ give the projected amount of money on deposit with the bank over the next $$12$$ months with and without the proposed promotional campaign, respectively.

list.item: Determine the signs of $$D_{1}^{\prime}(t)$$ , $$D_{2}^{\prime}(t)$$ , $$D_{1}^{''}(t)$$ , and $$D_{2}^{''}(t)$$ on the interval $$\left( {0,12} \right)$$ .

What can you conclude about the rate of change of the growth rate of the money on deposit with the bank with and without the proposed promotional campaign? Details Two curves y = D_1(t) and y = D_2(t) are graphed in the first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled t (months) and vertical axis is labeled y (\$). There is a single mark labeled 12 on the horizontal axis. From this mark, a vertical line rises upward parallel to the y axis. Both the curves begin at the same unlabeled point on the y axis, above the origin. The curve y = D_1(t) rises upward to the right, slightly bulging downward and reaches the line at t = 12. The curve y = D_2(t) rises gradually to the right, almost parallel to the x axis but slightly bulging upward and reaches the line at t = 12.

solution.paragraph: With or without the proposed promotional campaign, the deposits will increase; with the promotion, the deposits will increase at an increasing rate; without the promotion, the deposits will increase at a decreasing rate.

problem.paragraph: In the following figure, water is poured into the vase at a constant rate (in appropriate units), and the water level rises to a height of $$f(t)$$ units at time $$t$$ as measured from the base of the vase. The graph of $$f$$ follows. Explain the shape of the curve in terms of its concavity. What is the significance of the inflection point?

image.alt: Details Two images. The one on the left is a transparent concave cylinder, a cylinder with its sides caved inwards, almost half filled with water. The height of the water level from the bottom of the vessel is labeled f(t). The image on the right is a curve graphed in the first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled t and the vertical axis is labeled y. The curve starts from the origin, rises upward to the right bulging towards the horizontal axis. This region is labeled Concave upward. The curve then briefly rises linearly at a marked point labeled Inflection point. The curve then rises again to the right, bulging away from the horizontal axis.

solution.paragraph: $$f(t)$$ increases at an increasing rate until the water level reaches the middle of the vase at which time (corresponding to the inflection point) $$f(t)$$ is increasing at the fastest rate. The water rises faster when the vase is narrower. After that, $$f(t)$$ increases at a decreasing rate until the vase is filled.
